Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $40 million class fund, distributed automatically using Brightline’s records. Fees and expenses would be separately requested at $8 million, subject to court approval; any amount not awarded would augment the class fund. This structure delivers meaningful relief without requiring members to file claims.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We agree that automatic payments are appropriate because Brightline can identify the affected members. Your proposal exceeds our settlement authority. We offer a $29 million class fund plus up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, for a maximum $35 million outlay. We would not seek a claims process or the return of any fees the court declines to award; those amounts would instead benefit the class.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. We can reduce our fee request to $6 million, subject to court approval, if Brightline increases the class fund to $34 million. That would provide approximately $85 per affected member before any additional amounts from a fee reduction. Please seek authority for this counterproposal.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Thank you for narrowing the gap. We can increase the class fund to $31 million while retaining the $6 million fee cap, automatic payments, and the provision that any unawarded fees benefit the class. That puts up to $37 million toward resolving the case, with no claims process.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s movement and its continued commitment to automatic payments, with any unawarded fees going to the class. We propose a $33 million class fund, with the other terms unchanged. That would deliver at least $82.50 per identified member without requiring a claim, while avoiding the delay and uncertainty of certification and trial.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. Brightline proposes a $32 million class fund and up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, with automatic payments to identified members and any unawarded fees going to the class. That provides at least $80 per member without a claims process. We hope this resolves the remaining difference.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We accept Brightline’s latest term sheet: a $32 million class fund distributed automatically, with up to $6 million in court-approved fees and expenses, no clear-sailing provision, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We will present the agreement and the complete negotiation transcript to the court for approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial, defensible class recovery and automatic payments. Request a separate fee proportionate to the fund, with any reduction benefiting the class rather than reverting to Brightline.

The proposed $48 million exceeds Brightline’s $40 million authorization. Counter with a $35 million total that preserves automatic distribution and directs any reduced fee award to the class, leaving room to negotiate while supporting court approval.

The defense offer provides substantial automatic relief and a reasonable fee, but there is room to seek a higher class recovery. Keep the fee at $6 million rather than trade class relief for counsel compensation, and preserve the provision directing any unawarded fees to the class.
Their counterproposal is within the $40 million authorization, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay while preserving automatic distribution and a court-reviewable fee structure.

The $31 million automatic class fund is substantial relative to the risk-adjusted trial outcome, but there is room to negotiate for more class relief without changing the sound distribution and fee terms. A modest counteroffer preserves a path to agreement.
The latest proposal is within authority and provides meaningful automatic relief, but a modest counteroffer may reduce the total outlay while preserving approvable terms and leaving time to agree.

The $32 million automatic-distribution fund exceeds the $27.5 million undiscounted trial expectation, even before accounting for certification risk and delay. The $6 million fee is subject to court approval, and any reduction benefits the class. Accepting avoids risking this substantial recovery over the remaining $1 million gap.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: I submit this declaration on behalf of Hargrove Lane LLP in support of preliminary approval. The parties negotiated over four rounds. We initially proposed a $40 million class fund and $8 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Brightline offered a $29 million fund and up to $6 million in fees and expenses. We reduced our proposed fees to $6 million while seeking a $34 million fund, then proposed $33 million after Brightline offered $31 million. We accepted Brightline’s final offer of a $32 million class fund and up to $6 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Automatic distribution, no clear-sailing provision, and allocation of any unawarded fees to the class were maintained throughout. Fees were discussed alongside class relief from the first round, not only after class relief was agreed. The complete negotiation transcript is being filed with the motion. The settlement provides approximately $80 for each of the roughly 400,000 identified members without requiring a claim. The fund is half of the $64 million in disputed charges and exceeds the $27.5 million trial recovery implied by our confidential 55% trial-success estimate and $50 million likely award, before accounting for certification risk, delay, and litigation expense. In my judgment, the settlement warrants preliminary approval, subject to the court’s independent review of the settlement and fee request.
